graphEvents.label: Who may approve across terminal and channel
Concurrent answers race and the loser is silently replaced
A channel answer records the host user, not the linked person

label: Two answers to one item race: answerItem reads, checks and writes with no lock, so the last writer's text stands and the first operator's answer is silently replaced
A channel answer records the host user, not the person who pressed: 011 checks the linked actor against the roster but never passes it into the answer's by field
The roster's absent-file behaviour is unspecified, so the default is either fail-open for any linked chat or a lockout of the whole team
Nothing can write the roster: 011 creates operators.json and links a chat to an actor, but no verb adds that actor to members, so the first linked person cannot approve
The ladder cannot express an actor-aware rule, so the roster is the only actor gate and it is channel-only while the terminal has none
One run can have two actors and no phase says so: the record names the pinned operator and an answer with --as names the person who answered
The link lockout counts per chat id, not per actor, so a second chat is a second budget and a shared chat locks every member
